To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a single model of the problem to be solved is insufficient to achieve the best algorithmic results.
(1) the model is not the world, and that (2) algorithmic researchers must be careful not to over-interpret their results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms and data structures for the efficient solution of computational problems.
the design of algorithms and the development of tools to support their design and analysis.
the design and analysis, as well as the experimental study, of algorithms for problems in computer science and operations research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algorithmic research is a field of computer science, which is not a field of mathematics.
the model is not an algorithm, but rather a model of an algorithm.
algorithmic research has been successful, but that its successes are often overestimated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are interested in the design and analysis (both theoretical and experimental) of algorithms and data structures for a wide range of problems, including but not limited to the following topics: (1) Algorithms for massive data sets; (2) Algorithms for massive graphs; (3) Parallel and distributed algorithms; (4) Approximation algorithms; (5) Online algorithms; (6) Computational complexity; (7) Algorithms for computational geometry; (8) Algorithms for data mining and machine learning.
we are trying to make the design and analysis more efficient, more systematic and less error-prone by providing a framework of tools and techniques.
the algorithmic approach is a very successful approach to the design of algorithms, but it is not the only approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the algorithmic approach can be a very effective method for achieving speedups, but it is not a silver bullet.
, in the presence of a model, the algorithmic research community is incentivized to focus on the model rather than the problem.
the model is an abstraction of a real system, and that the algorithm designer must be aware of the limitations and assumptions of the model, and of the consequences of violating these assumptions.
